bullets.title: Market rebounds: S&P +0.2%, NDX futures +0.7–1% as semis stabilize ahead of NVDA earnings
bullets.body: U.S. equity futures extended gains to 0.7–1% on the Nasdaq 100 after tech suffered its largest de-grossing in two years. VIX sits at 15.69 with S&P at 7,670. The tape is broadening — 8 of 11 sectors rose on Monday despite SPX closing lower, with healthcare (+7.5% in August) and financials leading. High-beta momentum strategies are down another 3.5% and posting lower highs on NDX.

bullets.title: Jackson Hole / Warsh speech and PCE on deck as key catalysts for rates direction
bullets.body: Markets are watching Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole address later this week and July PCE data Wednesday. July Fed communication provided little clarity; investors expect potential market-moving commentary on whether easing cycle is over. 2-year Treasury yield returned to bullish above 4.20%, suggesting CPI re-acceleration risks and potentially tighter-for-longer expectations.

bullets.title: Bessent Treasury buyback plan: short-squeeze setup vs. Druckenmiller skepticism
bullets.body: Treasury Secretary Bessent is expanding bond buybacks targeting the long end, with CTAs near multi-year short extremes in Treasurys — BofA expects buybacks to push the 30-year below 5% while JPM warns this is price management, not liquidity management. Druckenmiller publicly criticized the intervention, arguing rising borrowing costs reflect structural fiscal problems that buybacks cannot fix. 10-year yield is near 4.65–4.68%, 30-year hit 5.34%.

bullets.title: Oil down ~3%, yields dip 3–4 bps as Iran geopolitical risk moderates
bullets.body: Brent and WTI fell over 3% to one-week lows after Pakistan-Iran diplomatic talks and signals that the U.S. is returning diplomats to Middle East embassies, easing conflict risk. The oil decline is putting downward pressure on long-end yields; Hedgeye flipped WTI to bearish on Trade/Trend. Lower oil is supportive of a disinflationary tape near term.

bullets.title: US sanctions 60+ Iran-linked entities ('Operation Economic Outcast') but spares major Chinese banks
bullets.body: Bessent announced sanctions targeting over 60 entities tied to Iran's oil, nuclear, and missile programs. Major Chinese and international banks were excluded despite China buying >80% of Iranian oil, preserving optionality ahead of a potential Trump-Xi summit. Beijing warned of potential retaliation but tone is measured.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler AI capex accelerating past cash flow; >$3.1T in off-balance-sheet commitments flagged
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley estimates hyperscaler AI capex will exceed $1.2T in 2027 vs ~$1T operating cash flow, funded via leases, debt, and equity. Combined NVDA + hyperscaler + AVGO off-balance-sheet commitments and guarantees exceed $3.1T through 2028. JPM separately flags risk premia across equities, credit, and rates are compressed, with equity multiples entirely dependent on the AI capex cycle continuing.

bullets.title: WFE estimates raised sharply: $223B in 2027 (+37%), $254B in 2028; DRAM bit supply +38% in 2027
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley raised wafer fab equipment forecasts to $223B in 2027 and $254B in 2028, driven by HBM4, DRAM, and leading-edge foundry capex. Goldman Sachs raised 2026–28 WFE forecasts 6–13% to $150B/$218B/$281B. China semiconductor capex plans are up 79% with $82B projected spending by 2030 for self-sufficiency. DRAM bit supply growth expected at 38% in 2027 vs 24% in 2025.

bullets.title: OpenAI Jalapeno chip outperforms NVDA/AMD/GOOGL on inference benchmarks — market share risk for AI chip leaders
bullets.body: SemiAnalysis reports OpenAI's proprietary Jalapeno inference chip outperforms NVIDIA, AMD, and Google chips on top open-source model benchmarks, with its general-purpose design delivering high performance across all inference scenarios. NVDA shares pulled back from highs on the report; implications for long-term custom ASIC competitive dynamics are significant.

bullets.title: NVDA credit risk flagged: ~$200B all-in exposure by CY28 via lease backstops and revenue-sharing models
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley initiated NVDA credit coverage at Neutral, estimating ~$200B all-in credit exposure by CY28 including $170B in adjustments and contingent obligations — the stock trades like BBB, not AA. JPM separately highlighted NVIDIA using $230B in lease backstops and residual guarantees to sustain demand, drawing comparisons to Lucent's vendor-financing collapse. NVDA Groq 3 LPX is in full production with Samsung ramping ~10K wafers/month.

bullets.title: META launches 'Hatch' AI agent platform at $199.99/month; 'Watermelon' model due October
bullets.body: Multiple sources confirm META is rolling out Hatch, a consumer AI-agent platform, within weeks at up to $199.99/month with higher usage limits and task automation. META is also developing the Watermelon model targeting an October release, and a WhatsApp AI-agent platform. This is a significant monetization step for META's AI infrastructure investment.

bullets.title: GOOGL TPU estimates raised sharply: $84B/$108B Cloud revenue in 2027/2028; Cloud to be ~50% of EBIT by 2028
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley raised GOOGL TPU pricing to ~$27B per GW (from $20B) at 30% gross margin (from 20%), implying $84B/$108B in TPU-related Cloud revenue for 2027/2028 — 35% above prior estimates. Brian Nowak targets $18–20 EPS in 2028 with Cloud reaching ~50% of total EBIT. Energy/utilities analyst team also raised TPU estimates with GOOGL expected to sell 0.3 GW TPU in 2H26, scaling to 4.2 GW by 2028.

bullets.title: August ISM tracking 56% on solid capex/manufacturing; Conference Board confidence dips to 89.4
bullets.body: PSC Macro: August ISM tracking a healthy 56% headline with regional capex plans at cycle highs, though Richmond Fed ISM-equivalent came in at 53.7 vs 53.3 prior and manufacturing headcount fell into contraction. Conference Board headline confidence edged down to 89.4 in August; jobs differential improved sharply with 'plentiful jobs' rising to 27.0% from 24.4%. Consumer inflation expectations ticked back up to 5.8%.

bullets.title: New home sales fell 10.5% m/m in July to 607K; prices at cycle lows, down 15% from Oct 2022 peak
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley data shows new home sales dropped 10.5% m/m in July to 607K vs MS estimate of 625K, with Midwest sales -43% m/m accounting for ~5ppt of the decline. New home prices fell 2.3% in July to a cycle low, down 15% from the October 2022 peak. Case-Shiller National Home Price Index rose 1.5% y/y in June and MS expects +2% y/y by year-end. 3Q real residential investment now tracked at -2.0% q/q saar but 3Q GDP tracking unchanged at 2.2%.

bullets.title: ETF flows: Government Bond ETFs see largest inflows; U.S. Large Cap ETFs post largest outflows
bullets.body: For the week ended 8/21/26, government bond ETFs recorded the largest inflows while U.S. large-cap equity ETFs posted the largest outflows after turning negative. Separately, Hedgeye added OIH and SLV to its model portfolio while selling SMDV and trimming QTUM and EPHE — consistent with a rotation away from tech/semis and into commodity-linked and dividend-focused assets.

bullets.title: Copper ETF (COPX) up 55% since October vs NVDA unchanged — materials outpacing AI narrative
bullets.body: COPX is up 33% YTD vs NVDA +12% YTD, and up 55% since October vs NVDA flat. China's data center electricity usage is set to quadruple by 2030 (exceeding South Korea's current consumption), reinforcing materials and energy infrastructure as the overlooked beneficiary of the AI build-out cycle.

bullets.title: S&P earnings breadth strong: 467 SPX companies report +50% aggregate y/y EPS growth
bullets.body: With 467 S&P 500 companies having reported, aggregate y/y EPS growth stands at +50%. Market breadth is expanding with 61% of stocks higher despite recent index-level weakness driven by semiconductor concentration. SPX immediate-term risk range is 7,601–7,825 with all-time highs still in play per Hedgeye's TRR target of 7,825.

bullets.title: Japan debt costs hit record $230B next fiscal year; German business confidence improves but real activity -10% below pre-Covid trend
bullets.body: Japan's Finance Ministry expects debt-servicing costs to surge 17% to ¥36.6T ($230B) next fiscal year on rising yields, adding a global sovereign pressure vector. In Europe, German Ifo business climate rose +2.1ppt to 88.8 in August but real GDP remains 10% below pre-Covid trend despite nominal GDP hitting record highs; PSC models point to softer activity in 2027:H1 as fiscal stimulus lags.

bullets.title: US-China agree to promote AI and trade cooperation; US-China 'Track 1.5' dialogue held in Beijing
bullets.body: Xinhua reports US and China agreed to promote cooperation in AI and trade, with a 'Track 1.5' diplomatic dialogue held in Beijing. Morgan Stanley separately characterizes the US-China relationship as 'stabilizing, not normalizing.' The near-term implication is that large Chinese bank exposure to Iran sanctions is being managed carefully to preserve the bilateral relationship ahead of a potential Trump-Xi summit.

bullets.title: Wolfe forecasts 65K August payrolls vs 55K consensus; ADP weekly data shows hiring acceleration
bullets.body: Wolfe Research expects 65K August payroll gains (above 55K consensus) with private payrolls +75K and government payrolls -10K; unemployment seen rising modestly to 4.16%. ADP weekly data for 4 weeks ending 8/8 shows average +11.75K private sector jobs, up from +9.5K prior — the second consecutive week of sequential acceleration. Job-seeking intention rose to 24.9% in July from 22.5% in March per NY Fed.

bullets.title: 22V warns AI capex financing at $7T debt scale could trigger meaningful inflation and yield pressure
bullets.body: 22V Research flags that AI debt financing — estimated at $7T in debt and $12T total through 2030 — could trigger significant inflation if implemented in an environment of equilibrium unemployment and elevated legacy inflation, risking meaningfully higher 10-year yields. DRAM market remains undersupplied through potentially 2028 but the memory basket's 2-year forward PE has already dropped below the 25th percentile as investors price in post-2028 supply risk.
